request: What is air made of? Let me guess the pie chart of nitrogen, oxygen and argon. #interactive #short
subtitle: Share out the pie: how much of the air you breathe is nitrogen, oxygen and argon? Then see where carbon dioxide's tiny sliver fits.

spec.title: What is the air you breathe made of?

sources.title: Trends in atmospheric carbon dioxide
sources.finding: CO2 is about 420-425 ppm (about 0.04 %), up from about 280 ppm before 1750

sources.title: Atmosphere of Earth
sources.finding: dry air is 78.08 % nitrogen, 20.95 % oxygen, 0.93 % argon, about 0.04 % carbon dioxide

commands.speak: Take a breath. What is that air actually made of?

ask.question: How is the air split? Drag the dividers to share out the pie.
ask.right: Close: off by {g.off} points on average.

commands.speak: Nitrogen is the giant: seventy-eight percent of every breath.
And it goes straight back out again: our bodies can't use it at all.
Oxygen, the gas we actually need, is only about a fifth.
Nearly all the rest is argon, a gas so unreactive that its name comes from the Greek for lazy.
And carbon dioxide, the gas behind global warming?
About 0.04 percent: four molecules in every ten thousand.
Tiny, yet that share has grown by half since before the industrial age.
